chapter_guidelines.content:
Z37.0, Single live birth, is the only outcome of delivery code appropriate 
for use with O80.
chapter_guidelines.title: Outcome of delivery for O80

chapter_guidelines.content:
complication 
Code O80 may be used if the patient had a complication at some point 
during the pregnancy, but the complication is not present at the time of 
the admission for delivery.
chapter_guidelines.title: Uncomplicated delivery with resolved antepartum complication

chapter_guidelines.content:
delivery 
Code O80 should be assigned when a patient is admitted for a full-term 
normal delivery and delivers a single, healthy infant without any 
complications antepartum, during the delivery, or postpartum during the 
delivery episode. Code O80 is always a principal diagnosis. It is not to be 
used if any other code from chapter 15 is needed to describe a current 
complication of the antenatal, delivery, or postnatal period. Additional 
codes from other chapters may be used with code O80 if they are not 
related to or are in any way complicating the pregnancy.
chapter_guidelines.title: Encounter for full term uncomplicated delivery

chapter_guidelines.content:
Codes from category O09, Supervision of high-risk pregnancy, are 
intended for use only during the prenatal period. For complications 
during the labor or delivery episode as a result of a high-risk pregnancy, 
assign the applicable complication codes from Chapter 15. If there are no 
complications during the labor or delivery episode, assign code O80, 
Encounter for full-term uncomplicated delivery. 
 
For routine prenatal outpatient visits for patients with high-risk 
pregnancies, a code from category O09, Supervision of high-risk 
pregnancy, should be used as the first-listed diagnosis. Secondary 
chapter 15 codes may be used in conjunction with these codes if 
appropriate.
chapter_guidelines.title: Supervision of High-Risk Pregnancy

Encounter Summary:
- 32-year-old G2 at 39 weeks gestation had a spontaneous vaginal delivery of a live male infant weighing 3350 g.
- Documentation states the labor was uneventful with blood loss 200 mL.
- Apgar scores were 10 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes.
- Postpartum recovery was good, breastfeeding was documented, and discharge occurred on day 3.
- Diagnosis documented: “term spontaneous vaginal delivery, singleton, live infant.”

Documentation Gaps:
- No significant CDI query opportunities identified from the excerpt.
  - Why it matters: The documentation already supports an uncomplicated term singleton liveborn vaginal delivery.
  - Evidence: “39 weeks gestation,” “spontaneous vaginal delivery,” “Labor uneventful,” and “Diagnosis: term spontaneous vaginal delivery, singleton, live infant.”
  - Minimal clarification needed: None clearly required based on the excerpt alone.
- Coding note rather than provider gap: outcome of delivery is supported and should be captured.
  - Why it matters: Outcome of delivery coding is required with O80 per coding guidance.
  - Evidence: “live male infant” and “singleton, live infant.”
  - Minimal clarification needed: None; single live birth is already documented.
- Coding note: gestational age is documented.
  - Why it matters: Specific weeks of gestation are available in the note.
  - Evidence: “39 weeks gestation.”
  - Minimal clarification needed: None.

Proposed Provider Queries:
- None recommended.
  - Reason: The excerpt supports an uncomplicated full-term spontaneous vaginal delivery with singleton live birth, and there is no clear ambiguity requiring provider clarification.
  - Supporting evidence: “Labor uneventful,” “blood loss 200ml,” and “Diagnosis: term spontaneous vaginal delivery, singleton, live infant.”

Coding Specificity Checklist:
- Delivery type documented: spontaneous vaginal delivery.
- Term status documented: 39 weeks gestation / term.
- Fetal count documented: singleton.
- Outcome documented: live infant / single live birth.
- Complication status documented: uneventful labor, good postpartum recovery.
- Neonatal details present but generally infant-focused: male infant, 3350 g, Apgars 10/10/10.

Risk Flags:
- No contradictions identified within the excerpt.
- No unsupported maternal complications documented.
- Avoid querying for obstetric complications, anemia, postpartum hemorrhage, perineal laceration, fetal distress, or other conditions because the excerpt does not provide supporting evidence.
